authorization: The owner's decision of 2026-09-28 (docs/platform/programme/DECISIONS-2026-09-28.md, §2; finding F-20) gives transit calendar feeds random opaque ids stored server-side, and says the privacy page will say what is stored, where, for how long, and how to remove it, in every locale that has it; only the listed sentences change. In each listed privacy page, in the section on the daily brief, calendar and notifications: two new paragraphs on what a subscription stores (the ten planets' positions and the whole-degree ascendant and midheaven, in Supabase's Tokyo region, with the times it was made and last fetched, under an address that carries only a random identifier), how long (until 12 months without a fetch), and how to remove it ("Remove this calendar" in the same browser, or by email), with the weekly backups' 90 days; the first sentence of the chart-code paragraph, now about calendar addresses made before random addresses; and that paragraph's last sentence, on replacing an older calendar address, replaced by a paragraph on those addresses' 60 days, the event asking to subscribe again, and what follows. Elsewhere on the page: the hosting-log sentence on what a calendar's address carries; the cookies paragraph's list of browser storage, which adds the addresses of calendars and the keys that remove them, and, after that list, two new sentences on what the browser that subscribed keeps for each calendar (its address, which lets anyone who has it read the calendar, the key that removes it, and when it was made) and that they stay until the calendar is removed there or the site's data is cleared in that browser, even after the server has deleted the calendar, as the independent review of this work on 2026-09-29 asks (its finding 11); and the list of choices, which adds removing a calendar. Every one of these sentences that the claims extractor selects is listed in docs/claims/ledger.json with its claim and evidence. The release chores in docs/OWNER-SETUP-RUNBOOK.md §8a step 4 also authorize changing only the updated and modifiedAt date lines on the four listed privacy pages to the UTC release day, currently planned as 2026-10-01; if the deployment moves to another UTC day those same date lines must be re-dated with LEGACY_FEED_WINDOW_START before the final rebuild and captures.
